title: Finite-Tor domains of the objects and test objects of the Poincare comparison
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $r,n\geq1$, $q=p^r$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its algebraic closure $k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, separated of finite type, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $a:X\to s$ be the structure morphism, with the exceptional admissibility and operations of [def-pod-conventions]. Use completed operations integrally, their scalar localization over $E$, and their common finite coefficient-stage versions over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x].

Put
$$C=Ra_!K,\quad\omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s,\quad L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega),\quad D=Ra_*L,\quad H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s),$$
with $Ra_*$, $Ra_!$, $Ra^!$ the derived, compact-support and exceptional operations of [def-pod-conventions] and internal Hom and tensor the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].
Then $C,D,H\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ and $\omega,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Moreover, for every $T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, both $La^*T$ and $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}La^*T$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Here $D^b_{ctf}$ is the bounded constructible finite-Tor category of [def-pod-conventions] at the chosen stage: at $\mathcal O_E$ the derived-complete integral category with the completed operations, at $E$ its scalar localization, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the common finite coefficient-stage category, with the specified coefficient-passage operations; no unbounded exceptional adjoint and no properness of $X$ is assumed. In particular $T=D$ and $T=H$ are admissible test objects, and the finite-Tor hypotheses of the projection formula and of the restricted tensor--internal-Hom and exceptional adjunctions hold for the pairs $(K,T)$, $(K\otimes^LLa^*T,\Lambda_s)$ and $(C,\Lambda_s)$.

proof.text: The structure map $a:X\to s$ is separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, as stipulated in the geometric datum. The coefficient unit $\Lambda_s$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$: at finite level it is a constant free rank-one complex in degree zero, of Tor interval $[0,0]$. Integrally its normalized reductions are those same units, all in $[0,0]$; at field stages use its integral representative. This verifies the finite-Tor definition at every stage.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: 'Put C=Ra_{X!}K, omega=Ra_X^!Lambda, and D=Ra_{X*}RHom_X(K,omega)'; second paragraph: 'its pullback and its tensor product with K are in the stated finite-Tor domains', extended from T=Lambda[-r] to all finite-Tor test objects, including D and H

proof.text: At $A_{E,n}$, apply clauses (i)--(v) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability]: pullback, tensor, internal Hom, ordinary and compact-support direct image, and the constructible exceptional inverse image preserve $D^b_{ctf}$. At the integral stage clause (vii) identifies $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$ and gives Hom and exceptional preservation; [lem-sf-package-coefficient-domain-realization] gives preservation by completed pullback, completed tensor and both direct images. The same two statements give the specified scalar-localized and common-stage operations at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Thus these closure assertions apply at the chosen stage, without an ambient exceptional adjoint.

proof.text: Apply step 2 successively: $K\mapsto Ra_!K=C$ and $\Lambda_s\mapsto Ra^!\Lambda_s=\omega$ give $C$ and $\omega$ in their asserted categories. The pair $(K,\omega)$ gives $L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega)$; then $L\mapsto Ra_*L$ gives $D$. Finally the pair $(C,\Lambda_s)$ gives $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$. All inputs have been checked before each application. General internal-Hom preservation suffices, so no claim that $C$ is site-perfect on an arbitrary scheme is needed.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: 'Put C=Ra_{X!}K, omega=Ra_X^!Lambda, and D=Ra_{X*}RHom_X(K,omega)'; second paragraph: 'its pullback and its tensor product with K are in the stated finite-Tor domains', extended from T=Lambda[-r] to all finite-Tor test objects, including D and H

proof.text: For any $T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, step 2 first gives $La^*T\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and then $K\otimes^L La^*T\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. In particular substitute the already established objects $D$ and $H$ for $T$. The projection-formula inputs $K,T$, the tensor--Hom inputs $K,La^*T,\omega$ and $C,T,\Lambda_s$, and the exceptional-adjunction inputs $K\otimes^L La^*T,\Lambda_s$ therefore have exactly the required finite-Tor membership. This proves the claimed domain conditions; no identification of $Ra_!$ with $Ra_*$ is used.
